- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.5) and price is rising, model often overshoots — cap forecast peaks at 1–2% below recent high or use moving average smoothing.  
- Model consistently underestimates price in early 30-day forecasts when sentiment is volatile — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to initial forecast if sentiment swings sharply.  
- If last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion (price bouncing back after dip), model often fails to recognize — apply slight upward bias to forecast if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model tends to lag behind true price movements — especially after sharp spikes — use 1–3 day lag correction: shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is bullish.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.4 → -0.3 → +0.4), model overfits short-term noise — apply smoothing filter or reduce volatility weight in forecast.
